1. **Outside view.** Google Trends search interest for a highly seasonal consumer tech product like the iPhone is defined by a massive, sharp spike during the product announcement week (usually mid-September) which sets the index to 100 for the trailing 12-month window. The baseline search volume during the rest of the year—driven by people looking for tech support, cases, older models, or replacement phones—tends to hover stably around 35 to 45 relative to that peak. A naive extrapolation for late summer, when search volume is generally at a low baseline, would predict an index in the low 40s. 

2. **Inside view.** The target week is Sunday, August 23 to Saturday, August 29, 2026. The snapshot will be taken on September 1, 2026, meaning the 12-month trailing window comfortably includes the previous year's September 2025 event peak (setting the 100 mark). However, late August is not just a typical baseline week. Apple historically sends out its media invitations for the September event during the last week of August (e.g., Aug 29 in 2023, Aug 26 in 2024). This routinely sparks a mini news cycle, driving a surge in rumor-related queries. This event-invite bump should elevate the index slightly above the summer trough, pushing it up by about 4 to 8 points. Therefore, we should expect a value in the mid-to-high 40s.

3. **Pre-mortem.** If this forecast is badly wrong, it is likely because the "invite bump" was either entirely missed by mainstream searchers (leaving the index at a flat trough of ~35) or it triggered a much larger, viral rumor cycle that caused the index to swell into the 60s. Alternatively, if the late August week happens to perfectly overlap with an early event date, it might spike even higher, though Apple rarely holds the event itself before September 7. I will use a moderately wide standard deviation to account for the variance in how much mainstream traction the event invites and rumors receive in any given year. 

4. **Calibrate.** A mean of 46 with a standard deviation of 8 implies approximately a 68% confidence that the actual index will land between 38 and 54. This range effectively covers a flat late-summer trough on the low end and a strong rumor-driven pre-event spike on the high end, providing a well-calibrated distribution.
